source.notes: Every signature below was read out of the interop assembly's own metadata and its decompiled declaration. The interop assembly carries declarations only: what a member does inside the game cannot be read from it, and nothing here claims otherwise.

targetKinds.entryPoint: ProjectileManager.WantToSpawnGlueOnEnemyAgent(uint syncID, EnemyAgent enemy, int limbID, Vector3 localPos, GlueVolumeDesc volumeDesc, float effectMultiplier)
targetKinds.signature: public static void WantToSpawnGlueOnEnemyAgent(uint, EnemyAgent, int, UnityEngine.Vector3, GlueVolumeDesc, float)
targetKinds.replication: The call builds the manager's own `pSpawnGlueOnEnemyAgent` packet and the game sends it through `SNet_BroadcastAction<pSpawnGlueOnEnemyAgent> m_spawnGlueOnEnemy`; the matching receive path is `ProjectileManager.DoSpawnGlueOnEnemyAgent(pSpawnGlueOnEnemyAgent)`, and the manager also keeps `SNet_Packet<pSpawnGlueOnEnemyAgent> m_recallSpawnGlueOnEnemyAgent` for a late joiner. Both are declarations read from metadata; the send/receive behaviour itself is a game-internal call edge that this file does not claim to have traced in the native binary.
targetKinds.syncIDSource: ProjectileManager.GetNextSyncID() -> uint (public static, declared in the same type). The glue launcher's own `pFireGlue` packet carries a `syncID:uint` of the same kind, so the id this row consumes is the manager's own sequence and not a value Forge invents.
targetKinds.limbID: The parameter the entry point calls `limbID` is the glue target's own index: `pSpawnGlueOnEnemyAgent.targetSubIndex` is packed from it, and `IGlueTarget.GlueTargetSubIndex` is the value that names which of an enemy's glue targets a spawn lands on. This row declares no port for it, so the call carries -1, the entry point's own 'no particular target' value, instead of this layer choosing a limb on the author's behalf.
readback: Dam_EnemyDamageBase.AttachedGlueVolume -> float (public getter) — the volume currently attached to this receiver, which is the only observable a void entry point leaves behind.
Dam_EnemyDamageBase.AttachedGlueRel -> float (public getter) — the same volume as a fraction of the receiver's own capacity.
Dam_EnemyDamageBase.IsStuckInGlue -> bool (public getter/setter) — the stuck flag the glue state machine drives.
Dam_EnemyDamageBase.GlueMoveSpeedMulti -> float (public getter) — the movement multiplier the attached volume produces.
targetKinds.record: Dam_EnemyDamageBase.AddToTotalGlueVolume(GlueGunProjectile proj, GlueVolumeDesc volume) is the receiver-side add the packet lands on. It is public and takes the projectile as a first argument; this provider does not hold a `GlueGunProjectile` and passes none, because the volume the plan asked for is the whole payload this row carries.

targetKinds.nativeEntryPointExists: ProjectileManager.WantToSpawnGlueOnDoor(uint syncID, pStateReplicatorProvider pDoor, int doorPartSubIndex, Vector3 localPos, GlueVolumeDesc volumeDesc)
targetKinds.whyNotImplemented: The entry point's `pDoor` argument is a `SNetwork.pStateReplicatorProvider`, and the only declared way to obtain one is `IGlueTarget.GlueTargetDoorSyncStruct`. `LG_SecurityDoor` exposes `GetSyncStruct() -> pStateReplicatorProvider` and `GetGlueTarget(int) -> IGlueTarget`, and `LG_Door_Sync` declares `m_syncStruct` and `GetGlueTarget(int)`, but the door instance itself is reached only through ForgeMap's own `map-object` address space. The framework has no entry point that turns another provider's entity reference back into that provider's native object (the object -> entity direction exists as `RuntimeModule.ObjectEntityResolvers` / `RuntimeKernel.ResolveEntity(object)`; the reverse does not), so this provider cannot resolve a door recipient at all.
targetKinds.evidenceForTheGap: Modules-ASM.dll declares no type whose interface list contains `IGlueTarget`: a metadata scan of all 3393 type definitions finds `IGlueTarget` itself and no implementor. The interface is therefore only reachable through whichever native object the game hands over, which is exactly the object this package cannot name.

targetKinds.whyNotImplemented: The entry point takes a world position, and no position exists anywhere in this row: its recipients are entity references, and the action declares no geometry port. Applying foam at a coordinate the author never gave would be a second, invented target. The row is therefore enemy-only until a geometry port exists.

targetKinds.nativeEntryPointExists: ProjectileManager.WantToSpawnGlueOnStaticEnemy(uint syncID, uint staticEnemyID, Vector3 localPos, GlueVolumeDesc volumeDesc)
targetKinds.whyNotImplemented: Its recipient is a `staticEnemyID`, the id of a `StaticEnemy`/`Dam_StaticEnemyDamage` instance. No provider in this tree registers a `gtfo.*` entity kind for static enemies, so a plan cannot name one and this row has no recipient to resolve.

volumeDescriptor.layout: explicit, three floats at offsets 0, 4 and 8

fields.name: volume
fields.meaning: The amount of foam this application carries, in the game's own glue unit — the same unit `Dam_EnemyDamageBase.AttachedGlueVolume` publishes and `AgentModifier.GlueStrength` / `AgentModifier.GlueEfficiency` scale.

fields.name: expandVolume
fields.meaning: The potential the volume may grow by. This row sets it to the requested volume: one number the author gave, not a second one invented for it.

fields.name: currentScale
fields.meaning: The projectile's own growing scale. It belongs to a projectile in flight, which a direct call has none of, so it is left at zero exactly as this package's other neutral native arguments are.

volumeDescriptor.notDeclaredInInteropTypeList: The type is absent from `ilspycmd -l c` output because that listing covers classes; its definition is present and decompiles on demand (`ilspycmd -t GlueVolumeDesc`). The test project's `GameDoubles.cs` declares it from the same metadata.

duration.evidence: The glue is added by volume and taken back by volume: `Dam_EnemyDamageBase.AddToTotalGlueVolume(GlueGunProjectile, GlueVolumeDesc)` and `RemoveGlueVolume(float deltaToRemove, float duration = 0f)` plus `ClearGlue()`. `ProjectileManager` declares `WantToMergeGlue(uint mergeTargetSyncID, float volume, float expandVolume)`, `WantToMergeGlueToNothing(uint mergeTargetSyncID)` and `WantToDestroyGlue(uint syncID)` — merging and destruction are explicit calls, not a schedule. No declared member takes an expiry, an interval or a tick count.
duration.consequence: A Forge-side `duration` is honoured by this provider itself: the applied volume is remembered per enemy life and removed by the same amount when the duration runs out, through the receiver's own `RemoveGlueVolume`. The ledger keeps no native state of its own beyond that record.

stuckInGlueStateMachine.note: The glue state machine is the enemy's own: `ES_StateEnum.StuckInGlue` is a movement state the enemy enters on its own once enough volume is attached. This row therefore does not drive it — it writes volume, which is what the launcher does too — and no `state_request` is issued for it.

hostClient.reason: `SNet.IsMaster` is the authority gate every write in this provider already uses. The glue entry point is a static 'want to' call whose replication is the manager's own broadcast, so a client that reached it would ask the game to send a spawn the master never authorized.
hostClient.clientVisibility: Not established by this file. Whether a client sees the glued enemy's slowdown is a game-internal consequence of the broadcast; it is listed under gameConfirmations rather than claimed.

volume.reason: One native unit is a float; a non-finite, zero or negative volume is not a small amount of foam. The ceiling matches the range the package's other numeric action ports use.

strength.reason: The game's own launcher passes its own positive multiplier. Zero and negatives are refused rather than passed through.

duration.reason: Ticks; zero means the game's own behaviour, which is no timer.

resultCodes.authority-or-phase: not the host, or the provider is not in a phase that may write
resultCodes.volume-out-of-range: the volume is not one the entry point can carry
resultCodes.strength-out-of-range: the strength is not one the entry point can carry
resultCodes.duration-out-of-range: a negative duration, or one that would overflow the tick count
resultCodes.too-many-targets: more recipients than the result-row budget
resultCodes.stale-or-unsupported-recipient: the reference is not a current enemy life of this provider
resultCodes.missing-glue-receiver: the recipient holds no glue receiver, or it does not read
resultCodes.glue-receiver-owner-mismatch: the receiver belongs to another enemy instance
resultCodes.glue-budget: the provider's own live-application cap is reached
resultCodes.foam-handle-unavailable: the kernel refused the effect handle the dispatch needs
resultCodes.native-commit-exception: the spawn entry point threw; the spawn may or may not have been sent
resultCodes.receiver-changed-during-commit: the life or the receiver changed while the spawn ran
resultCodes.readback-exception: the readback after the spawn threw
resultCodes.unexpected-glue-readback: the receiver read back a volume below what it held, or did not read at all
resultCodes.glue-unseen: the entry point ran and the published volume did not move — a dropped spawn and a receiver already at its cap are indistinguishable from here

gameConfirmations: Whether `WantToSpawnGlueOnEnemyAgent` is accepted on the host for an enemy the master does not own, and what the broadcast does on a client.
Whether the volume a client publishes after the broadcast equals the host's `AttachedGlueVolume`.
Whether `RemoveGlueVolume(deltaToRemove, 0f)` removes exactly the volume that `WantToSpawnGlueOnEnemyAgent` added, or whether the receiver's own merge/decay changes the amount in between.
Whether a spawn at the entry point's `-1` sub index lands on the enemy's first glue target, and what a `limbID` beyond the enemy's glue target count does.
Whether `GlueVolumeDesc.expandVolume` equal to `volume` is a sane authoring default or whether the launcher's own expansion ratio should be reproduced.
